title: Relative dual abelian spaces and normalized Poincare identities
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $A\to S$ be a proper smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation whose geometric fibres are abelian varieties [def-trf-algebraic-space]. An abelian variety here is a smooth proper geometrically connected group scheme over a field. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; smoothness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. A line module means an $\mathcal O$-module on the small etale site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O$; on a scheme it corresponds to an ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Rigidified means equipped with a specified trivialization at the identity section.

There is a dual group algebraic space $A^\vee\to S$ of the same kind and a universal line module $\mathcal P_A$ on $A\times_SA^\vee$. For every $S$-scheme $T$, maps $T\to A^\vee$ classify line modules on $A_T$ algebraically trivial on all geometric fibres and rigidified at the identity, up to rigidification-preserving isomorphism. Algebraic triviality on a geometric fibre means equivalence to the trivial module under the equivalence relation generated by pairs of fibres of a line-module family over a connected smooth parameter variety. The universal module is canonically trivialized on both identity axes, with the same trivialization at their intersection. For every $S$-scheme $T$ and every line module on $A_T$, any automorphism preserving an identity rigidification is the identity, whether or not that line module is algebraically trivial.

The normalized Poincare module is biadditive: on $A\times_SA\times_SA^\vee$ and $A\times_SA^\vee\times_SA^\vee$, respectively,
$$(m_A,1)^*\mathcal P_A\simeq p_{13}^*\mathcal P_A\otimes p_{23}^*\mathcal P_A,\qquad (1,m_{A^\vee})^*\mathcal P_A\simeq p_{12}^*\mathcal P_A\otimes p_{13}^*\mathcal P_A.$$
Here $m$ denotes addition and $p_{ij}$ the indicated projections; the isomorphisms preserve the identity-axis trivializations. For any line module $L$ on $A$, let $q:A\times_SA\to S$ and $e:S\to A$ be the structure and identity maps. The normalized difference family
$$N_L=m_A^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*L^{-1}\otimes q^*e^*L$$
defines a group homomorphism $\phi_L:A\to A^\vee$ by $x\mapsto[t_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}]$, and $N_L\simeq(1\times\phi_L)^*\mathcal P_A$ with both axis trivializations.

For every homomorphism $a:A\to B$ between such spaces, pullback of line modules defines $a^\vee:B^\vee\to A^\vee$, and there is a canonical axis-preserving isomorphism $(a\times1)^*\mathcal P_B\simeq(1\times a^\vee)^*\mathcal P_A$. The dual spaces, universal modules, their rigidifications, these identities and these isomorphisms commute with every base change between locally Noetherian schemes, including geometric fibres. Their canonical comparisons satisfy identity and composition.

source.place: I §8, printed pp.36--40, universal Poincare module and normalized difference family; I §9, printed p.41, dual homomorphism. Relative algebraic-space form is the duality input implicit in Deligne, Le lemme de Gabber, §4.1, printed pp.141--142; this generalization is a statement-only prerequisite, not claimed proved by the field-only Milne theorem.

proof.text: On etale scheme charts smoothness gives flatness by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Each geometric fibre is geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], applied to the abelian variety in the hypothesis. Thus [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] applies to $A\to S$ with section $e_A$, producing the separated locally finitely presented group space $P$ of all rigidified line modules, its universal module $U$, and $\mathcal O_T\simeq(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{A_T}$ for every $T$. It also proves the asserted automorphism statement for every rigidified line module, without imposing algebraic triviality.

source.place: Tags 0D28, 0D2B, 0D2C, with 0E0S and 0DNJ as stated in the Picard prerequisite

proof.text: For an algebraically closed geometric residue field $K$, the fibre $A_K$ is projective by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective] and geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization]. The full Picard representation in [lem-sfb-projective-picard-identity-representability] therefore identifies $(P_K)^0$ with the functor of rigidified algebraically trivial families. The same functor is represented by the smooth proper connected dual abelian variety in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]; hence $(P_K)^0$ is smooth and proper. Given a square-zero lifting problem into $P$ whose geometric images are in these components, the universal module converts it into exactly the lifting problem of [lem-sfb-abelian-picard-infinitesimal-lift]. Its etale-local lifts give lifts into $P$ by [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-proper-neutral] to obtain $D=P^0$, proper smooth and finitely presented over $S$, with geometric fibres the field duals. Its functor is precisely the fibrewise algebraically trivial rigidified families. Set $A^\vee=D$ and $\mathcal P_A=U|_{A\times D}$.

source.place: I sections 8--9; relative assembly by the worker

proof.text: The universal rigidification trivializes $\mathcal P_A$ on $e_A\times D$. The zero of $D$ represents the trivial rigidified module, so representability gives the trivialization on $A\times e_D$ whose value at $(e_A,e_D)$ is the prescribed one. Any two rigidification-preserving isomorphisms of a family differ by an automorphism, which is the identity by [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard]. On a product of copies of $A$ and $D$, every global unit comes from the base. The space $D\to S$ of step 2 is flat on etale scheme charts by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and its geometric fibres, being abelian varieties, are geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization]; with its zero section, [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] therefore applies to $D$ as well as to $A$. Apply its universal structure-sheaf pushforward assertion successively to the projections, which are base changes of $A$ or $D$ along a product of the others; when that product is an algebraic space, apply it on an etale scheme chart and glue, since global units form an etale sheaf. Thus an automorphism of the trivial line on an identity axis is fixed by its value on the remaining identity section. Consequently an isomorphism normalized on one axis, if it exists and respects the other at their intersection, respects that whole axis. Its restriction there is such a unit, and its identity value makes it 1.

source.place: I sections 8--9; relative assembly by the worker

proof.text: For $L$ on $A$ form $N_L$ exactly as in the statement. Pulling to either identity axis cancels $L$ with $L^{-1}$ and $e^*L$ with its dual, giving the two canonical trivializations. On a geometric fibre, the family parameterized by the connected smooth variety $A_K$ connects the fibre at any point to its trivial fibre at the identity. Thus every parameter fibre is algebraically trivial, by the stated definition. The representing property of [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] and the subfunctor description in [lem-sfb-smooth-group-proper-neutral] give $\phi_L:A\to D$ and the normalized isomorphism $N_L\simeq(1\times\phi_L)^*\mathcal P_A$. The zero parameter gives $\phi_L(0)=0$. Now [lem-sfb-relative-abelian-pointed-rigidity] makes $\phi_L$ a group homomorphism. The fibre description is the class of $t_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}$ with the identity-line normalization in $N_L$; the displayed shorthand does not omit that normalization.

source.place: I sections 8--9; relative assembly by the worker

proof.text: Apply the difference construction of step 4 to the universal module in the $A$ variable. It defines $F:A\times D\to D$: its value at $(y,z)$ is the rigidified translated difference of $\mathcal P_{A,z}$. Existence as a morphism follows from [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] and [lem-sfb-smooth-group-proper-neutral], since on every geometric fibre the translation parameter in the connected smooth variety $A_K$ connects this difference to zero. Both $F(0,z)$ and $F(y,0)$ are zero, by the normalizations. The product assertion of [lem-sfb-relative-abelian-pointed-rigidity] gives $F=0$ as a morphism, including over a nonreduced base. The representing property now identifies its rigidified family with the trivial family. Undoing the definition of the difference gives $(m_A,1)^*\mathcal P_A\simeq p_{13}^*\mathcal P_A\otimes p_{23}^*\mathcal P_A$. For the second identity, addition in $D\subset P$ is tensor product, so $(1,m_D)^*\mathcal P_A$ and $p_{12}^*\mathcal P_A\otimes p_{13}^*\mathcal P_A$ represent the same family. The uniqueness from step 3 makes both isomorphisms preserve all identity axes.

source.place: I sections 8--9; relative assembly by the worker

proof.text: For $a:A\to B$, pull a rigidified family on $B$ back by $a\times1$. Since $a(0)=0$, rigidification pulls back. Pulling back every family in a chain defining algebraic equivalence preserves that chain, and tensor products are preserved. Thus the representing property of [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard], with the neutral subfunctor of [lem-sfb-smooth-group-proper-neutral], yields the homomorphism $a^\vee:B^\vee\to A^\vee$. The two pullbacks of universal modules in the statement classify this same rigidified family, so their unique normalized isomorphism gives the desired comparison. Finally for $S'\to S$, a rigidified family on $A_{S'}\times_{S'}T$ is exactly one on $A\times_ST$; algebraic triviality is tested on the same geometric fibres. Base change for the Picard representation and the neutral subfunctor therefore identifies $D_{S'}$ with the dual for $A_{S'}$. Universal modules, their axes and the difference construction pull back by their explicit formulas. Each comparison is characterized by the rigidified family it represents. Identity and either composite comparison represent the same family, and uniqueness in [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] makes them equal, proving all the asserted coherences.
